Hi Alison — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a draft order-form clause and a residency matrix for the classes you called out. Ben and Monica are cc'd to confirm operational/engineering details.

1) 48-hour residency for PII-derived embeddings (US hosted): yes — we can commit to a 48-hour maximum residency for that class as an addendum to the order form. This will be implemented via a combination of TTL enforcement and prefix-aware KV cache invalidation.

2) Purge orchestration / evidence: we provide machine-generated purge receipts (JSON audit artifacts) and a human-readable wipe certificate (PDF) after the job completes. The receipts include request id, impacted object ids, start/end timestamps, node set, and cryptographic hash of the deletion manifest.

3) Exports vs deletion: exports created prior to a deletion request remain subject to your retention controls; however, we can include a rule in the order form that scheduled bulk deletions will also invalidate eligible export snapshots created within the last X hours (proposed 24 hours) to avoid a window of accessibility.

Next steps: Ben will propose exact SLA language and timelines (including escalation SLAs), Monica will propose audit log fields and evidence delivery cadence, and I'll consolidate into an Order Form redline for you.

Regards,

Thanks — quick operational detail thread.

Ben here (DSR and infra coordination): implementation approach we recommend for the 48-hour PII-derived embeddings window:
- Ingest tagging: we tag objects at creation with the "CW-PII-emb" class.
- Active cache eviction: continuous prefix-aware eviction ensures no KV cache hit after TTL expiry; background sweep runs every 30 minutes; worst-case KV TTL drift < 60 minutes.
- Long-term store: blob manifests are queued for deletion at 48 hours; deletion workers process manifests with parallelism and confirm via receipts.

For the 72-hour purge SLA you suggested: we can guarantee purge completion on primary and replicated blob storage within 72 hours of a validated purge request for data classes covered by the order form. That SLA excludes third-party backups and archives unless explicitly enumerated in the order form.

On receipts & proof: receipts will be stored in your audit log bundle for 365 days (accessible via the Console API). Format: request_id, objects_processed_count, start_ts, end_ts, node_ids, deletion_manifest_hash, operator-id (system). We can also provide an optionally-signed wipe certificate for renewal/attestation.

Open question for legal: do we need to commit to scrub of cross-region replication copies for hosted customers, or will a contractual exclusion suffice? Markus, can you advise.

-ben
Ben Carter

Legal perspective / recommended order-form language (high level):

1) Residency commitment: "Redwood will ensure that specified customer data classes marked in Schedule A (e.g., PII-derived embeddings) will not be retained in searchable runtime caches or long-term storage beyond the bespoke residency window specified in the Order Form, except for residual copies created by standard backup processes or as required by law."

2) Purge SLA & scope: "Redwood will complete purge operations for the specified data classes within 72 hours of a validated purge request. Purge operations include cache eviction, manifest deletion, and object removal from primary and configured replicated stores. Purge of external third-party backups or archival exports will only be included if expressly listed in Schedule B."

3) Evidence delivery: Redwood to provide a machine-readable purge receipt within 24 hours of completion and a signed human-readable certificate within 5 business days. Audit logs with request_id and checksum will be retained for 365 days and accessible via an API endpoint.

4) Limited liability and verification: include a verification process (customer-provided audit token) and an indemnity carve-out for data present in customer-controlled exports or transfers initiated by the customer.

If Cloudwell accepts the above at a high level, I'll produce a redline for the Order Form (Schedule A/B) and a short definition section for "purge", "residency window", and "evidence".

-Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
